# About the Report

The Sustainability Report of PT Super Bank Indonesia Tbk (henceforth referred to as "Superbank," the "Bank," or "We") reflects our evolving sustainability journey. Following a full year of steady progress focused on capacity building, we are proud to share our latest developments with our stakeholders. Designed to be clear, accessible, and easy to understand, this report is based on a materiality assessment that we reviewed and validated more comprehensively in 2025, serving as the foundation for our Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance. In this report, the terms "Sustainability" and "ESG" are used interchangeably.

## Disclaimer and Limitation of Liability

This report contains forward-looking statements regarding Superbank's future conditions, strategies, initiatives, and plans, which are prepared based on management's assumptions, estimates, and judgments at the time of this report's publication. Such statements involve risks, uncertainties, and other factors that may cause actual results or performance developments to differ materially from those projected.

The information in this report is for informational purposes only and does not constitute, nor should it be construed as, investment, tax, legal, or financial advice. PT Super Bank Indonesia Tbk does not act as an advisor or fiduciary in this capacity. Any investment decisions or actions taken based on the content of this report should be consulted with an independent professional financial, legal, or tax advisor.

## Reporting Period, Regulatory Compliance, and International Standard References

This report covers the period from January 1 to December 31, 2025, and outlines Superbank's strategic approach, key initiatives, and achievements in conducting its operations across Indonesia. This report was prepared with reference to Financial Services Authority Regulation (POJK) Number 51/POJK.03/2017 regarding the Implementation of Sustainable Finance for Financial Service Institutions, Issuers, and Public Companies, Financial Services Authority Circular (SEOJK) Number 16/SEOJK.04/2021 regarding the Form and Content of Annual Reports of Issuers or Public Companies. In line with the implementation of international best practices, Superbank also adopts the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) Standards and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) as frameworks to monitor and measure ESG performance.

## Publication

This full report was published on April 2026, and is available on our website in PDF format, in both Indonesian and English.

## Contact Us

If you have any questions or would like to provide feedback regarding this report or ESG-related matters, you may contact sustainability@superbank.id.

In 2025, Superbank underwent a significant transformation in its status and structure through an Initial Public Offering (IPO), marking its transition into a public company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange. This change carries material implications for heightened standards of transparency, accountability, and public disclosure obligations.

Additionally, Superbank was reclassified as a KBMI 2 bank following an increase in core capital exceeding Rp6 trillion. This reclassification has strengthened the bank's capital structure and enhanced its ability to manage risks and support sustainable business growth.

Building on this foundation, Superbank's 2025 sustainability strategy focuses on integrating Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles across all operational lines. Superbank consistently aligns business priorities with sustainable practices through prudent governance and disciplined risk management, ensuring readiness to navigate regulatory dynamics and meet the expectations of customers, investors, the public, and regulators.

# SuperGROW: From Aspiration to Culture

The SuperGROW aspiration remains the primary compass of our sustainability journey. This theme is not merely a slogan, but a tangible embodiment of the company's core value, "Make an Impact." We believe that true sustainability is born when innovation and social responsibility converge in every business decision.

To that end, we are committed to continuing and maximizing the implementation of SuperGROW across the Bank's activities. Through ongoing internalization programs, we ensure that the principles of People, Profit, and Planet are understood and practiced by every stakeholder at Superbank. Consequently, sustainability is no longer a separate initiative but a standard of conduct that defines how we work and serve, in order to create meaningful long-term value for a better future.

Promoting sustainable digital banking by developing climate governance and risk management within the banking portfolio, eco-friendly operations, and smart green offices, by reducing our environmental impact while simultaneously promoting responsible finance.

# Super-Reliable and Safe

Ensuring data privacy and digital security, delivering a secure and regulatory-compliant digital banking experience, and supporting the creation of a safe, healthy, and supportive work environment for all employees.

# Super-Opportunity

# President Director's Remarks and Explanation on the Sustainability

## Dear Valued Stakeholders,

The year 2025 marks the beginning of a transformative new era for Superbank. Our successful debut on the Indonesia Stock Exchange as a public company, coupled with our elevation to the KBMI 2 bank category, stands as a testament to our evolving business maturity. To us, attaining public company status is more than a corporate achievement; it is a mandate to uphold high standards of transparency and accountability. This transformation serves as a primary catalyst for us to solidify our comprehensive Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) framework, ensuring that every stride of future growth is resilient, responsible, and creates long-term value for all our stakeholders.

The implementation of sustainable finance at Superbank is built upon a foundation of mature risk governance and compliance with regulatory expectations. In 2025, Superbank successfully completed its inaugural Climate Risk Management & Scenario (CRMS) stress test to ensure the resilience of the Bank's business model against various transition and physical risk scenarios.

Through this initial implementation, we have gained critical insights into how climate scenarios may impact our portfolio resilience, credit quality, and long-term financial performance. This achievement strengthens our foundation in climate-related risk governance and aligns our practices with OJK's expectations and emerging global standards.

## 1. Policies to Address Challenges in Achieving the Sustainability Strategy

In responding to the dynamics of the 2025 sustainability landscape, marked by global macroeconomic complexities and escalating climate risks, Superbank has taken strategic steps by proactively strengthening its risk management architecture. To mitigate the increasingly tangible impacts of both physical and transition risks, the Bank responsively completed its Climate Risk Management & Scenario (CRMS) stress test to precisely assess credit portfolio resilience and secure long-term business model sustainability amidst environmental uncertainty.

Meanwhile, Superbank's transformation into a public company is embraced as strategic momentum to accelerate organizational governance and accountability standards to a higher level. Addressing the urgent need for internal competency in this new era, the Bank moved swiftly to align human resource capabilities through intensive and targeted ESG capacity-building programs across various functional lines. This strategic response is institutionally reinforced through the establishment of the Sustainability Policy and the integration of the SuperGROW framework, ensuring that sustainability principles are not merely compliance activities but are deeply embedded as strategic pillars in every operational decision-making process of the Bank.

## 2. Sustainable Finance Implementation

To fulfill our mission of creating a 'Lasting Impact' for society and the environment, Superbank adopts a holistic approach to implementing Sustainable Finance principles. We realize this commitment through our SuperGROW strategy, a sustainability aspiration ecosystem designed to address global challenges while meeting local needs. Through this strategy, we ensure that sustainability is not merely a theoretical concept but is deeply embedded in every service interaction and business decision we make.

# A. Super-Green: Commitment to Green and Sustainable Operations

The Super-Green pillar reflects Superbank's dedication to realizing a digital banking service that is not only technologically advanced but also environmentally responsible. We implement smart green office concepts to maximize energy efficiency and promote the prudent use of resources. Beyond internal efficiency, we minimize our carbon footprint through digital technology innovations that enable financial services without physical boundaries. This commitment is further strengthened by the development of a green portfolio and sustainable finance practices focused on climate-conscious investments, serving as an environmental risk mitigation effort for long-term sustainability.

## A.1 Environmental Risk Analysis & Climate Governance

The year 2025 marks a new milestone in Superbank's sustainability journey with the successful completion of our inaugural risk stress test (CRMS). Using 2024 as the baseline year, this stress test recorded a Scope 2 emissions efficiency performance of 146.86 tCO2e. This achievement provides a robust data foundation to anticipate the impacts of climate change on the resilience of our credit portfolio and future financial performance. We view this inaugural CRMS initiative as the first step in a long-term journey toward climate governance maturity. Moving forward, Superbank is committed to:

a. Continuously refining methodologies and data quality for climate risk analysis to align with global standards and OJK regulations.
b. Deeply integrating climate considerations into the Bank's strategic planning and risk management.
c. Identifying long-term energy efficiency opportunities to support the transition toward low-emission operations.

## A.2 Innovation for Sustainable Eco-Friendly Business

We actively expand our financial support for environmentally oriented businesses, including through strategic participation in the Grab Ventures Velocity program. Through a collaboration with Jejak in, an environmental technology platform, we have realized the planting of 400 verified trees as a tangible contribution to carbon offset initiatives. This partnership reinforces Superbank's vision to integrate technology, social impact, and sustainability, while continuing to open financing opportunities for green businesses in the future. Furthermore, the Bank held an inspiring knowledge-sharing session, titled "Path to Green and Inclusive Products," in collaboration with Grab Indonesia's sustainability team, which shared practical strategies for community empowerment through technology and sustainable initiatives.

## A.3 Smart Green Office: Cultivating a Sustainable Mindset

We believe that green transformation begins with daily habits. Therefore, Superbank implements various initiatives to foster environmentally conscious behavior among employees, including:

a. Plastic-Free Weeks: A monthly program that successfully reduced the use of more than 500 plastic bottles per month, supported by replacing bottled water with glass pitchers in meeting rooms.
b. Energy Efficiency: Encouraging an energy-saving culture by turning off unused electronic devices and implementing regular monitoring of electricity consumption.

## A.4 Eco-Friendly Operations: The Advantage of Digital Banking Services

As a technology-based institution, we leverage digital innovation to significantly reduce our environmental impact through three primary approaches:

a. **Branchless Operations**: Our digital technology enables customers to transact anytime without the need to visit a physical location. This directly reduces carbon emissions from customer travel and eliminates the energy consumption associated with conventional brick-and-mortar branch buildings.
b. **Paperless Culture**: We have optimally transitioned from paper-based administrative processes to a digital documentation ecosystem. This initiative spans from digital customer onboarding to internal documentation, aimed at reducing paper waste while simultaneously enhancing data security and workflow efficiency.
c. **Sustainable Cloud Infrastructure**: Superbank strategically utilizes cloud infrastructure instead of conventional physical servers. By partnering with global cloud providers committed to carbon-free energy, we ensure IT operations that are adaptive, secure, and significantly more energy-efficient than conventional data centers.

# B. Super-Reliable and Safe: Uncompromising Integrity and Security

The Super-Reliable and Safe pillar is a manifestation of Superbank's priority in maintaining security and operational integrity. This strategic foundation is built upon robust data protection, a comprehensive AML-CFT (Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Financing of Terrorism) program, and the creation of a safe and conducive working environment. Through the implementation of high-standard security systems and proactive illegal activity detection, we ensure a transparent, secure, and trusted banking environment for all our customers.

## B.1 Data Security and Protection: A Holistic Approach

Superbank provides digital banking services that place financial control in the hands of the customer, backed by a robust security infrastructure that protects data privacy in every transaction. Our integrated security approach is embedded across the entire business cycle, reflected in our operational governance, product development, human capital capabilities, and technology.

a. **Governance and Product Development**: Our commitment to responsible data management is enshrined in our transparent internal governance architecture (detailed in the 2024 Sustainability Report). In product development, we implement a "Shift Left Security" strategy, where security considerations are integrated from the initial design phase to mitigate risks as early as possible.
b. **Human Capital Capabilities**: We recognize that the best technology requires reliable operators. Therefore, Superbank invests heavily in international certifications for our information security team to navigate the evolving cyber threat landscape. Our team holds the following certifications:

- Management & Audit: CISSP, CISA, CISM, ISO 27001 Lead Auditor & Implementer.
- Technical & Operational: CEH, OSCP, Red Team Operator, Certified DevSecOps Professional.
- Data Privacy: CIPM, CIPP/E, and Certified Indonesian Personal Data Protection Officer (CIPDPO).

Furthermore, a strong digital security culture is fostered through mandatory employee training and periodic phishing simulations in compliance with OJK regulations, ensuring organization-wide vigilance.

c. **Technological and Cyber Resilience**: Superbank employs a defense-in-depth framework to prevent, detect, and respond to threats. Our infrastructure is protected by a 24/7 Security Operations Centre (SOC) utilizing advanced platforms (SIEM & SOAR) and cloud technology secured through VPC isolation and Web Application Firewalls. All customer data is protected using industry-standard encryption (AES-256 at rest and TLS 1.2+ in transit). This commitment is validated by our ISO 27001:2022 certification, confirming the implementation of international standards in information and cyber security.
d. **Customer Awareness and Due Diligence**: Security is a shared responsibility. We actively educate customers through regular campaigns on account protection and fraud trends. Internally, we apply rigorous due diligence principles, including both CDD (Customer Due Diligence) and EDD (Enhanced Due Diligence), in our customer onboarding and partner management processes to prevent financial crime and maintain the integrity of the banking ecosystem.

# B.2 Anti-Money Laundering, Counter-Financing of Terrorism, and Counter-Proliferation Financing (AML, CFT, and CPF)

Superbank strengthens its AML-CFT and CPF programs through a risk-based approach. This governance is executed via the "Three Lines of Defense" model:

a. First Line: AML Operations Unit under the Operations Director.
b. Second Line: AML Compliance Unit under the Compliance Director.
c. Third Line: Internal Audit Department providing independent oversight.

System Development and Strategic Plan: In 2025, we consistently enhanced our internal systems for transaction profile monitoring and regulatory reporting to PPATK (Indonesian Financial Transaction Reports and Analysis Center), while performing risk-based customer data updates (Risk-Based Approach).

# B.3 A Safe and Conducive Working Environment

For Superbank, a safe workplace means creating a culture where every individual feels respected and supported both physically and psychologically. This commitment received external recognition through a Bronze Award in the Best Employee Wellness Strategy category at the Employee Experience Awards Indonesia 2025.

We foster a positive work environment through various concrete initiatives throughout the year:

a. Anti-Harassment Education: "Creating a Safe & Respectful Workplace" sessions held with Bullyid to reinforce a "speak-up" culture and prevent discrimination.
b. Mental & Physical Well-being: A series of events for World Mental Health Day and Breast Cancer Awareness, including mindfulness yoga sessions, health seminars (Health Talks) on cancer, free health screenings, and emotional resilience workshops and book reviews.

# C. Super-Opportunity: Unlocking Access, Empowering Growth

The Super-Opportunity pillar reaffirms Superbank's commitment to being a catalyst for financial inclusion in Indonesia. We focus on providing access to financing for underbanked segments and Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) that have traditionally faced barriers within the conventional banking system.

To expand our sustainability impact, we strategically integrate banking services into leading digital ecosystems, including Grab, OVO, and KakaoBank. This collaboration allows us to serve a broader segment of society through seamless and rapid transactions. This commitment is bolstered by a solid network of loan partners, ensuring equitable capital distribution to create a sustainable economic impact.

# C.1 Empowering Communities and MSMEs

Financial inclusion is more than just access, it is the foundation of economic resilience. Through inclusive financial solutions and tailored lending, we empower individuals and business owners to achieve financial independence. Our empowerment strategy focuses on four dimensions of impact:

a. Economic Stability: Providing access to affordable credit for those marginalized from the formal system, helping them break the cycle of poverty and build a solid financial foundation.
b. Livelihood Improvement: Equipping MSMEs with financial tools that simplify operations, allowing entrepreneurs to focus on business expansion and create employment opportunities.
c. Technology-Driven Growth: Access to financing enables MSMEs to invest in technology and infrastructure, transforming small businesses into competitive entities.

d. Bridging the Gap: Ensuring banking services reach all layers of society regardless of background, creating an ecosystem where economic opportunities are equally distributed.

# C.2 Innovative Financing Solutions through Strategic Partnerships

Our alliances with loan partners are the keys of Superbank's social impact strategy. We provide financing products tailored to the specific needs of our customers:

a. Asset-Based Financing (Used Car Ecosystem): Collaborating with automotive fintech platforms to provide working capital for dealers (MSMEs) and purchase financing for end-customers.
b. Inclusive Multipurpose Loans: Providing flexible access to cash for underbanked individuals for both productive and personal needs.
c. Focus on Underserved Segments: Expanding our reach to the unbanked population, strengthening their ability to participate actively in the formal economic system.

# C.3 Financial Literacy: Building a Financially Savvy Generation

In 2025, Superbank's financial literacy initiatives reached 930 participants through both online and offline sessions. These initiatives involve Superbank employees directly educating the community on financial management and responsible digital banking.

Key Literacy Initiatives:

a. Dangdut Academy Partnership: A unique breakthrough by sponsoring a popular talent search show to reach the mass market segment. This program provided dedicated education sessions for the show's audience, introducing the benefits of digital banking in accessible language.
b. Youth Focus: Recognizing that the younger generation are digital natives, we organized interactive sessions for elementary, middle school, university students, and interns. The goal is to instill a financially savvy mindset from an early age so they are prepared to grow alongside Indonesia's digital economy.

# C.4 2025 Super-Opportunity Activities

a. Modal Mimpi & Masa Depan Event: A financial education and empowerment program for aspiring entrepreneurs.
b. Middle School Financial Literacy in Rajeg: An interactive session equipping middle school students with money management skills.
c. Education for Grab Partner's Children: A special event for the children of Grab driver-partners to introduce the concept of saving from an early age.
d. Banking 1-on-1: Intensive mentoring sessions for Superbank interns to help them understand the banking industry landscape.

# D. Super-Women: Inclusive Leadership and Gender Equality

The Super-Women pillar reaffirms Superbank's commitment that gender equality begins at the highest levels of leadership and extends to all aspects of organizational development. With strong female representation on our Board of Commissioners and Board of Directors, inclusivity is deeply embedded in our governance and decision-making culture. This foundation is further strengthened through capacity-building initiatives and entrepreneurship development programs designed to foster leadership and provide equal opportunities for all genders.

## D.1 Building an Inclusive and Responsive Work Environment

We believe that an inclusive work environment begins by recognizing and supporting the unique needs of every individual. Our strategy goes beyond mere regulatory compliance, focusing on providing fair remuneration and benefits as well as holistic wellbeing programs.

## D.2 Remuneration Equality and Flexible Benefits

Superbank implements a fair compensation policy for all employees, regardless of gender or employment status. In addition to standard benefits in accordance with applicable regulations, we pay special attention to employee health through various flexible supplementary benefits.

To support work-life balance, we provide the Flexi-Benefit program, which can be tailored to the personal needs of employees:

a. **Flexi Spending Account**: Funds that can be used for self-development, out-of-pocket healthcare costs, immediate family care, and work-related activity support.

b. **Flexi Wellbeing Account**: Includes a Mental Wellbeing Account and a Preventive Healthcare Account, which are specific allocations for early detection and health protection (medical check-ups and vaccinations) as well as psychological support, enabling employees to proactively prioritize their physical and mental health.

## D.3 Super Women and Allies Club (SWCA): A Space to Grow Together

## Occupational Health and Safety (OHS)

Workplace safety is fundamental to fostering a productive and healthy environment where employees feel secure and valued. This commitment demands the implementation of rigorous measures to mitigate workplace accidents, injuries, and occupational hazards. Key actions include providing adequate training, ensuring the availability of safety equipment, and maintaining an organized workspace. By upholding strict safety standards and regulations, the organization protects its workforce while reducing operational disruptions associated with workplace incidents. Generally, these safety procedures encompass various aspects, such as:

## Building Access

1. Restricted access for third parties/guests, with a requirement for a designated person-in-charge to meet and escort guests throughout their stay in the office.
2. Installation of monitoring devices (such as CCTV).
3. Periodic reviews of physical building access and workplace environmental controls to ensure safety, including fire detection and suppression, electrical data adjustments, air conditioning (HVAC) regulation, humidity control, and other related measures.

## Implementation of Occupational Safety

1. All work equipment must be stored in a secure location.
2. Prohibition of eating, drinking, and smoking in areas containing information storage facilities or computer centers (server rooms).
3. Provision of regularly updated emergency contact numbers, including the police, building security, fire department, ambulance, nearest hospitals, National Electricity Company (PLN), Regional Disaster Management Agency (BPBD), and others.
4. Fire risk protection by providing and maintaining fire suppression systems, water sprinklers, smoke detectors, and Portable Fire Extinguishers (APAR) in easily accessible areas, establishing disaster protection and office evacuation procedures in accordance with Business Continuity Management (BCM) and other relevant protocols, and storing flammable materials outside computer and communication rooms. With the support of the building management where we operate, fire drills are conducted regularly to ensure all employees can respond quickly and effectively in fire emergencies.
5. Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS) are compiled to provide information for all employees regarding potential hazards (health, fire, reactivity, and environmental impact) as well as guidance for working safely with chemical products.

Our dedication to providing a safe and healthy workplace is formalized through Superbank's comprehensive commitment to OHS compliance. We ensure this through ongoing adherence to regulatory mandates, meticulous implementation of safety protocols, and the promotion of a work culture that prioritizes awareness and accountability for the well-being of all personnel, contractors, and relevant stakeholders.

2. Savings Products:

Main Savings Account: An account that is automatically created when a customer successfully registers as a Superbank customer. Customers can use the Main Savings Account for sending and receiving transfers from other banks.

Saku by Superbank: Additional savings account designed to help allocate customers' money according to their specific needs. Saku can also be named to match the customer's allocation preferences.

OVO Nabung: Enables one-click account opening for Superbank's digital savings within the OVO app, offering interest rates of up to 5% p.a. with seamless transactions.

The amount saved will be adjusted based on the chosen deposit frequency by the customer. Customers have the opportunity to earn higher interest rate of up to 10% p.a. and the balance can be withdrawn at any time.

Deposito by Superbank: Savings product in the form of a deposit that can be accessed through the application, offering benefits with interest rates of up to 7.5% p.a. where the term can start as early as 7 days and can be withdrawn earlier before the maturity date without any administrative fees.

Superbank x Grab Integration: Integrates digital banking services into the Grab ecosystem through direct debit and in-app onboarding, enabling automatic payments, instant account opening within the Grab app, and same-day settlement for partners/merchants to drive the adoption of Superbank's services.

Lucky Pocket: Offers customers daily cash rewards by saving once and selecting a Lucky Pocket each day, with prizes credited directly to the main savings account and additional chances for customers who participate consistently for 7 consecutive days.
